Q1.question: Is the r5.2 → r6.2 failure a general cross-version failure?
Q1.answer: NO. r5.1 secondary-stress completed-window neural mean PR-AUC remains far above prevalence, so the r6.2 near-prevalence collapse is not shown to be a general CERT-version failure.

Q2.question: Does r5.1 show substantial cross-version ranking transfer?
Q2.answer: YES, descriptively. Neural completed-window mean PR-AUC on r5.1 remains orders of magnitude above prevalence, indicating retained ranking despite large absolute drop from r5.2 validation.

Q3.question: Is r6.2 qualitatively more severe than r5.1?
Q3.answer: YES. r6.2 neural completed-window PR-AUC sits near prevalence; r5.1 does not.

Q4.question: Is r6.2 failure predominantly ranking collapse, decision-threshold shift, or both?
Q4.answer: BOTH, with family dependence: neural ranking collapses to near prevalence, while all 18 frozen models show a large negative-class frozen-threshold exceedance shift on r6.2. Tabular families retain more ranking than the neural pathway but still fail at the frozen decision boundary.

Q5.question: Do RF/XGBoost retain more ranking portability than the neural pathway?
Q5.answer: YES, relatively, on r6.2 completed-window PR-AUC. This is descriptive relative portability, not a claim that tabular models succeed.

Q6.question: Does teacher anchoring show a reproducible predictive advantage over C2 across external versions?
Q6.answer: NO as a general predictive-superiority claim. Point deltas are small; several de-overlap PR-AUC intervals include zero; r6.2 deltas sit on a collapsed PR-AUC scale. A positive point estimate is not predictive superiority.

Q7.question: Does teacher anchoring show reproducible teacher-relative mechanism/fidelity preservation across external versions?
Q7.answer: YES on the exact-frozen metrics compared here (r5.1 and r6.2). C5 remains closer to the teacher than C2 on logit deviation, route MAE/KL, and agreement. r5.2 validation mechanism values are not included (provenance insufficient).

Q8.question: Which input/score shifts best distinguish r6.2 from r5.1?
Q8.answer: Largest |r6.2 mean − r5.2 TRAIN mean| features: email_count, has_file_activity, total_events. r5.1 scaled means remain close to r5.2 TRAIN. Score-side, r6.2 negative frozen-threshold exceedance rises from ~0.0003–0.001 on r5.2 validation to ~0.41–0.45, far above the r5.1 elevation.

Q9.question: What exact failure mechanism should EDITOR-008 attempt to address?
Q9.answer: A version-specific r6.2 representation/distribution shift that both destroys neural ranking and moves negatives across frozen r5.2 decision thresholds, while teacher-anchoring fidelity does not restore predictive portability. EDITOR-008 should treat shift detection, source-robust representation, and decision portability as required capabilities, with teacher anchoring auxiliary only. Do not freeze an architecture here.
